sentences.text: 7. On a query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties before Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi on 19.09.2019 and affidavits showing the protection of interest of minor child as per the judgment titled as Ganesh vs. Sudhirkumar Shrivastava, (2020) 20 SCC 787 passed by the Honble Supreme Court have been filed and the same are on record.
8.

It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner and other family members.
9. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- in three instalments in the following manner:

First instalment of Rs.2 Lakhs paid to respondent no. 2 in the first motion petition.
b. Second instalment of Rs. 2 Lakhs paid to respondent no. 2 in the second motion.
c. Third/Final instalment of Rs. 1 Lakh to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Honble High Court at New Delhi.

10. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 1 Lakh today, i.e., 08.11.2023 vide DD No. 049620 drawn on Union Bank of Indian and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

11. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion and also the fact that the present matter is a family matter, I am of the opinion that no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
Moreover, there is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.
